problems.quote: the diversity of an idea set as the ratio between the number of unique concepts it includes and the total number of ideas
problems.note: The reported outcome counts unique concept groups and divides their count by the number of ideas. Codebook section 6 explicitly assigns counts of unique ideas coded by clustering to category_count. Cosine similarity between Universal Sentence Encoder embeddings determines which ideas overlap; the outcome recorded here is the resulting unique-concept proportion, not an embedding distance or similarity score. Keep the embedding model and threshold in measure_detail. The percent units of the S3 body-text value do not change this measure classification.

summary: Checked all 11 estimates. Read the complete 462-line markdown conversion and all 10 pages of the main PDF, including its appended Reporting Summary. Opened every cited estimate page with pymupdf and consulted the original Lee and Chung methods (PDF pp. 6-8) to confirm inherited assignment and arms. All 14 non-null statistical entries match the cited PDF and the stated arms: nine 95% confidence levels, the S3 Human-only value of 100 percent, and sprinkler totals of 20 versus 12 and 20 versus 7. No numerical transcription or arm-assignment error was found. The S3 value is a percentage, not a fraction. Nine measure codes should be category_count because the outcomes are proportions of unique concept groups. Five additional diversity outcome families are absent from estimates and are reported as missing here; these five entries do not assert an unverified number of missing contrasts. The other reviewed coding fields are consistent with the accessible paper: across_people, diversity, set-level outcomes, immediate production with AI available, between-person assignment, appropriate active or unassisted comparators, and the stated directions. Sprinkler counts are lexical overlap totals, not participant means. Null people counts are not replaced by idea counts or original-study sample sizes. Figure-only arm values remain null under extraction rule 1. Supplementary Table 1 could not be read: Python urllib requests with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 to the named Springer supplement and https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/zf3s2/files/osfstorage/ both failed with WinError 10013. Filename searches in the library, repository, Downloads, D:/projects/ai-skill-atlas and accessible temporary files did not locate the supplement; some temporary directories were unreadable. Consequently, the complete contrast inventory and the uncertainty basis of the uniqueness comparisons remain unverified. The recorded not_reported uncertainty codes should not be taken as confirmation that the supplement reports no uncertainty. No unavailable statistics or additional AI-configuration contrasts were inferred.
